Division boundaries of a survey round

Source: R/map.R
bdhs_boundaries.Rd

The subnational (division) boundaries used for each Bangladesh survey, as an sf object. Boundaries change between rounds as divisions were created (Sylhet 1995, Rangpur 2010, Mymensingh 2015), so use the boundaries of the round you are mapping.

Usage

bdhs_boundaries(survey = 2022)

Arguments

survey

Survey references (see bdhs_survey_id()); several are allowed, and NULL returns every round.

Value

An sf object (EPSG:4326) with columns survey_id, region_code, region_name, unit_id (stable 4-digit code of the geographic unit across rounds), reg_id and geometry.

Details

Boundaries come from the DHS Program Spatial Data Repository (https://spatialdata.dhsprogram.com/home/, ICF), licensed under the Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0. region_code is the region code used in the recode files (v024/hv024), and reg_id links to the region_id of official subnational estimates in bdhs_official().

See also

bdhs_map()

Examples

b <- bdhs_boundaries(2022)
b
#> Simple feature collection with 8 features and 5 fields
#> Geometry type: MULTIPOLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 88.03243 ymin: 20.59039 xmax: 92.68078 ymax: 26.63625
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>   survey_id region_code region_name unit_id          reg_id
#> 1 BD2022DHS           1    Barishal    0001 BDDHS2022360001
#> 2 BD2022DHS           2  Chattogram    0003 BDDHS2022360003
#> 3 BD2022DHS           3       Dhaka    0010 BDDHS2022360010
#> 4 BD2022DHS           4      Khulna    0006 BDDHS2022360006
#> 5 BD2022DHS           5  Mymensingh    0011 BDDHS2022360011
#> 6 BD2022DHS           6    Rajshahi    0009 BDDHS2022360009
#> 7 BD2022DHS           7     Rangpur    0008 BDDHS2022360008
#> 8 BD2022DHS           8      Sylhet    0004 BDDHS2022360004
#>                         geometry
#> 1 MULTIPOLYGON (((90.33083 21...
#> 2 MULTIPOLYGON (((91.85583 21...
#> 3 MULTIPOLYGON (((89.35535 23...

#> 7 MULTIPOLYGON (((88.83978 25...
#> 8 MULTIPOLYGON (((90.96542 25...
